policy: Examples demonstrate reasoning, not templates or measured production outcomes.

examples.title: Developer workspace
examples.goal: Help developers manage work with fast repeated tasks.
decisions: Keep primary task navigation stable and make current scope explicit.
Use density only where it improves scanning.
Prefer authentic code or product artifacts over generic mockups.
tradeoffs: Dense workspaces need hierarchy and responsive alternatives.
acceptanceChecks: Users can identify current scope and next action.
Common tasks do not lose context.
Keyboard focus and error states are recoverable.

examples.title: Product-led SaaS landing page
examples.goal: Explain one capability and motivate a qualified next action.
decisions: Demonstrate value through an actual workflow.
Choose hero from product artifact and message.
Keep pricing and technical claims attributable.
tradeoffs: Product demo can need more space than short hero.
Expressive visual must not obscure comprehension.
acceptanceChecks: First viewport explains product and audience.

examples.title: Public service application
examples.goal: Help someone submit an application with confidence and error recovery.
decisions: Use plain language and explicit required cues.
Preserve values after recoverable errors.
Localize policy content to correct jurisdiction.
tradeoffs: A stepper helps long application but may burden short form.
Explanations aid confidence but can overwhelm.

examples.title: Editorial publication
examples.goal: Make long-form information easy to scan, navigate and understand.
decisions: Use constrained reading measure and clear hierarchy.
Let imagery support rather than interrupt.
Keep metadata and contents navigation useful.
tradeoffs: Display type adds personality; body text remains comfortable.
TOC helps long pieces but is unnecessary for short reads.
acceptanceChecks: Text reads on mobile and desktop.

examples.title: Commerce catalog
examples.goal: Help shoppers discover, compare and understand products.
decisions: Use consistent product imagery and useful product facts.
Filters reflect actual catalog attributes.
Price and variants are not fabricated.
tradeoffs: Editorial imagery must not hide comparison data.
Dense filters may need progressive disclosure on mobile.
acceptanceChecks: Price and variants are visible before purchase.
Filters work with keyboard and touch.

examples.title: Education learning path
examples.goal: Help learners understand progress, next action and feedback.
decisions: Show meaningful progress and lesson state.
Make feedback understandable and retryable.
Keep reward effects secondary.
tradeoffs: Gamification can motivate but cannot replace guidance.
One-task lessons need clear return path.

examples.title: Media discovery and playback
examples.goal: Help users find authorized content and control playback.
decisions: Separate controls, current item, queue and discovery.
Show truthful loading and unavailable states.
Do not imply availability without provider confirmation.
tradeoffs: Persistent player improves continuity but cannot obscure content.
Recommendations should be secondary when catalogue is limited.
